exposure: Subsequent deliveries in the same woman
outcome: Severity of shoulder dystocia in subsequent deliveries
Rates of planned cesarean section in subsequent deliveries
cohort: 1,091,067 pairs of first and second, second and third, and third and fourth births in the same mother, 824,323 mother-offspring pairs, and 614,663 father-offspring pairs from the Medical Birth Registry of Norway
finding: There is a strong recurrence risk of shoulder dystocia, especially severe, in subsequent deliveries in the same woman, and the inter-generational recurrence risk was higher on the maternal than paternal side.
mod_finding: Women with a history of shoulder dystocia, particularly severe shoulder dystocia, had higher rates of planned cesarean section in subsequent deliveries.
